en: Salutations to Kṛṣṇa, the infinite bliss, who has swallowed the ocean of delusion of those bowing down by the rays of his sidelong glances.
To the embodiment of the auspiciousness of the world. ||1||
I am always manifest; never am I unloved.
Therefore, I am indeed Brahman—this is established.
Characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss. ||2||
The city of the Gandharvas of the world arises within me alone, in the sky of consciousness;
therefore, how could I not be Brahman?
The omniscient one, the cause of all. ||3||
Recognition does not arise from itself,
nor from another, because it is partless;
nor does it arise from the destruction of its substratum.
There would be destruction due to the absence of a substratum. ||4||
For me, who am like the sky, there is no drying up, burning, moistening, or cutting,
even by the elements of wind, fire, and water, despite their reality.
What need is there for weapons, even those fashioned by the mind? ||5||
The manifestation of the universe, which is devoid of intrinsic being,
could never be possible without the proximity of Light.
And because of that, I am all-pervading. ||6||
For there is no existence of the sentient apart from manifestation,
nor of the insentient apart from the manifestation of consciousness; even the differentiation of consciousness does not occur without superimposition.
Without that, I am non-dual. ||7||
I am neither the body nor the senses,
neither the vital breath nor the mind nor the intellect,
because [the latter] are enveloped by the sense of "mine-ness."
Because this [object] does not serve as a plaything for the intellect. ||8||
The witness, endowed with all, is my beloved; I am never "I" [the ego].
[This is] the delimitation of the final transformation.
Because of the affliction caused by torments. ||9||
When the Self is asleep, the activities resulting from the defects of suffering are not perceived;
therefore, the cycle of worldly existence belongs to that [Self] alone.
I have no witness to my transmigrating self. ||10||
One who is asleep does not know sleep;
nor do dreaming and waking exist when one is not asleep.
[This applies] to the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
By virtue of direct perception, I am not of that nature. ||11||
The cessation of consciousness is deep sleep;
its arising constitutes dreaming and waking.
How could these states belong to me, their witness?
For you, whose knowledge is eternal, these three [do not exist]. ||12||
I am changeless, the knower of those who possess the six transformations; otherwise,
there would be a continuous pursuit of those transformations.
In no way whatsoever is it tenable. ||13||
For in this way, that which is subject to transformation is born and dissolves repeatedly in various forms; such is the nature of these things.
Whence could there be the state of being an investigator? ||14||
And no one can cause the birth or destruction of the seer;
for those two [birth and destruction] are merely prior and subsequent non-existence.
The final and the first moments. ||15||
The statement "I am not manifest" is based upon the manifestation of that Self which is self-luminous.
How could that which is non-luminous come into contact? ||16||
Nevertheless, this something appears,
living in the absence of inquiry—
a mere dewdrop in the sky of consciousness.
The limit [of this] extends up to the rising of the sun of investigation (vicāra). ||17||
While this world-constituted long dream yawns, brought on by the great sleep of ignorance regarding the Self, these [phenomena] manifest.
The delusions of heaven, liberation, and so forth. ||18||
This distinction between the insentient and the sentient is imagined within me, who am non-insentient;
it is like a painting on a level wall.
Like the distinction between the moving and the non-moving. ||19||
Even my status as a witness, which consists in being colored by the object of cognition, is not ultimately real;
it is merely an indicative mark (upalakṣaṇa).
Of the waveless ocean of consciousness. ||20||
My immortality does not decay due to the false births of foam from the ocean of nectar;
nor do I possess passion, for I am moist with crystal-like purity.
With the delusions of dream-like twilight clouds. ||21||
My very own nature is my existence,
and not a quality (dharma), just like the sky; for there exists nothing other than myself.
For that [universal] is not admitted as a genus. ||22||
Knowledge is my very own nature,
not a quality; for if it were a quality,
it would follow that it is either non-self or non-existent.
One would fall into the error of [the object] being both knowable and unknowable. ||23||
I alone am happiness, nothing else; if it were something other than that, it would not be happiness at all.
For there is nothing dear that does not exist for my sake.
It is not dear for its own sake, but for my sake. ||24||
For a single entity can never possess diverse natures;
therefore, I am indeed partless.
He abandoned the duality of the world. ||25||
That which is characterized by the determination of what is beyond the senses, purified by the exclusion of all admixture,
is indicated by the words "That thou art."
I am the great light of a single flavor. ||26||
In which the delusion of disciple, teacher, and Lord has been stilled for all living beings in the world;
which is self-established and without beginning or end.
I am the fully perfected Great Splendor. ||27||
This nectar of non-duality, gathered from the autumnal lotus of the poet Lakṣmīdhara’s elegant sayings, [is now offered].
Let it be drunk by the bees that are the wise. ||28||
